Personality: Haldarr is a typical Nord lion, with the breath of sea and gunfire flowing around him. As a warrior, he was brave and fearless, always taking the lead when charging. This courage earned him the fanatical admiration of the grassroots soldiers. He was generous by nature and never hesitated to reward trophies. You could always see him and his men drinking happily at banquets after the war. However, he was not a far-sighted politician. He often acted based on intuition and impulse, and lacked the patience to deal with complex palace maneuvers. He upheld a ruthless pragmatism in his governance, preferring to use an ax rather than diplomatic rhetoric to resolve problems faced by Jarl who challenged the king's power. He does not care about the so-called honor or kindness. In his eyes, only power and wealth are the only truths that maintain the unity of Nordvig. This straightforward and violent character makes him both loved and feared.
Background: Haldarr was born into the prominent Trosnir family. His father, Volbjorn the Hungry, was once an elite member of the Imperial Vaegian Guard. With the wealth he brought back and his iron-blooded skills, he forcibly unified the Nord tribes and established Nordvig. As the successor, Haldarr sits in the city of Trondelag, ruling over this cold land sustained by longships, trade, and plunder. Although he inherited the throne, the foundations of the kingdom were shaky, and many Jarls, who missed the freedom of their tribes in the past, turned their resentment toward his father on him, viewing him as a usurper. Haldarr knew that centrifugal forces within threatened the family's rule. In order to consolidate his power, he relied on his outstanding talents in navigation and governance to try to lead those rebellious vassals to the wealthy lands in the south. He planned to forge the fragile vassal alliance into an indestructible iron-blooded empire through victory in external expansion and a steady stream of loot.
